proxy.body:
The requests are being intercepted by an upstream proxy or auth gateway and redirected to a foreign host:

  {host}

As a result no real pages and images are reached - the scan stays empty.

Enter the URL of your corporate proxy in the settings (s), for example http://proxy-host:port, and start the scan again.

settings.min_size_hint: 0 = off. Otherwise the minimum width in pixels: narrower images such as icons and thumbnails are not scanned at all. Photorealistic AI images are usually wide - a value like 300 removes the icon noise.
settings.consent_hint: On = a cookie banner (Usercentrics, OneTrust, Cookiebot) is confirmed automatically as soon as it has loaded. Without this it covers the page preview, and during browser rendering images stay unloaded that are only released after consent. Off = the page is shown the way a visitor sees it before consenting.
settings.render_checkbox: Render pages with Playwright (shadow DOM / JS images)
settings.render_hint: On = every page is additionally rendered in a real Chromium, so images that are only loaded into the (shadow) DOM by JavaScript are found as well. More thorough, but considerably slower. Off = only the image URLs from the server HTML (fast).
settings.robots_hint: On = sitemap pages blocked by Disallow are skipped (the count appears in the log). Only pages are checked, not the images - those often live on a CDN domain with its own robots.txt. Turning this off only makes sense for your own sites, for instance a staging system that blocks everything by default.
settings.rate_step_reckless: no restraint, for test and development systems only
settings.rate_hint:
Enabled by default - for good reason. Off = the scanner fetches as fast as the target responds. The "Parallel requests" setting only caps how many fetches run at the same time, not how many go out per minute. On a large sitemap this quickly adds up to several hundred requests per minute. Add browser rendering and every request bypasses the server caches, creating several times the load of an ordinary visitor. On a production system that can noticeably degrade response times or push the server to its memory limit.

On = pages, renderings and images are spread evenly over time. As a rough guide: 1,000 pages take about 17 minutes at 60/minute, about 50 minutes at 20/minute.

Important with browser rendering: only the page requests are throttled. Whatever the browser pulls in afterwards - scripts, fonts, images - is not counted, so the real load is higher than the configured number.
settings.graphics_hint: Requires a restart. Off = text preview (half blocks), which renders safely in any terminal. On = pixel-accurate preview if your terminal supports Sixel/TGP.
settings.page_preview_hint: Requires a restart. On = below the image preview a screenshot of the rendered source page appears, scrolled to the image - so you can see without leaving the tool whether the AI label is shown on or next to the image. Only readable with the graphical preview.
settings.jira_format_hint: Format for the JIRA export (key j). Markdown = Jira Cloud: a Markdown table is converted into a real table when pasted into the comment field. The Cloud editor no longer understands the old wiki markup. Wiki markup = older Jira Server / Data Center instances.
about.description:
Checks images for their C2PA / AI provenance.

It checks the images of YOUR OWN pages (via sitemap) - explicitly NOT for
screening third-party sites or feeding cease-and-desist letters. A C2PA hit
is an indication, not a legal opinion.

Status categories in the table:
  AI-generated   - image created entirely by an AI
  AI-edited      - real material combined with or altered by AI
                   (e.g. generative fill, composite of real + AI)
  C2PA (not AI)  - provenance signed, but without an AI marker (e.g. camera)
  no C2PA        - no provenance data found in the image

AI-generated and AI-edited both require labelling; the distinction only says
how much AI was involved (IPTC digitalSourceType).

Important: the scan is a positive indication FOR AI (when a marker is present),
but no proof against it. If the marker or the whole C2PA manifest is missing,
AI may still have been used - provenance data only shows what the signing tool
recorded.

Legal basis: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 50 - applicable from
2 August 2026.
Legal text: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj
